digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III; Pakia (2005) App. VI

teaser.en: One of its Digo names simply means 'trap', because that is what its sticks become.

summary.en: *Mkete* is a small coastal forest tree of the fig family, with toothed leaves and white latex. Its sticks are made into traps, which gives it its other name, *msusu*.

about.en: *Mkete* is a small tree of the forest understorey. Its leaves have toothed edges, and like its relatives in the fig family it bleeds a white latex when cut.

where.en: It grows in coastal forest, in the shade of taller trees.

uses.en: The sticks are cut and made into traps, known as *susu*.

names.en: Pakia records two Digo names, *mkete* and *msusu*. *Msusu* means 'trap', after the traps made from its sticks; the same name is used in Swahili. No English name is in common use.

reason.en: Also named after the object made from it
Its name also means the tool made from it
Small fig-family tree named for its use

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
